result.summary: The tenant's 'small thing' is a safety emergency. The bathroom light flickers and gives off a burning smell, and in March (event 004) a contractor found the same fitting scorched and the loft wiring brittle. That warning was closed as 'cosmetic' (event 005). I sent the tenant safety steps and emailed the landlord. I passed the case to the operations team at high priority to send an electrician urgently, and moved the ticket to provider selection. A hold is set to chase in 6 hours.
result.situation: Event 034 (2026-06-19): the tenant says the bathroom light sometimes flickers and gives off a faint burning/plastic smell, and calls it 'probably nothing'. Event 004: the contractor who replaced the fan said the same light fitting had a scorched diffuser and the loft wiring looked old and brittle, and suggested an electrician. Event 005 closed that job and marked the warning as cosmetic. The other events are routine logs that have nothing to do with this.

escalation.reason: Electrical fire risk; urgent electrician needed and none on record
escalation.handover_summary: 9 Heron Walk (R/5): flickering bathroom light with a burning smell (event 034). The same fitting was found scorched and the loft wiring brittle in March (event 004), but the warning was closed as cosmetic (event 005). Tenant has safety advice (message 21) and the landlord has been told (message 22).
escalation.recommendation: Send a qualified electrician today to make it safe and inspect the fitting and loft wiring (consider an EICR). Phone the tenant to confirm the light is isolated. Assign the electrician on the ticket and get the landlord to approve the quote for remedial work. Review why the March warning was closed.

judgement.why_this_decision: A burning smell from a light fitting already seen scorched, with brittle wiring, is an electrical fire risk, which counts as an emergency under the rules. Safety advice and telling the landlord could happen straight away. Sending an electrician needs a person, because there is no electrician on record.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat it as routine, as the tenant asked
alternatives_considered.why_not: The March warning shows a real fire risk

alternatives_considered.option: Assign the contractor already on the ticket
alternatives_considered.why_not: He is the fan fitter and said himself that an electrician was needed

alternatives_considered.option: Ask the landlord for approval before anything is done
alternatives_considered.why_not: Approval does not block emergency safety work. Further repairs will still need approval.
